title: Scheme local finite presentation characterized by affine limit tests
statement:
Let $B$ and $U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g:U\to B$ be a morphism, and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Then $g$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] if and only if for every small nonempty directed set $I$ and every inverse system of affine $B$-schemes $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ with limit $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Mor}_B(T_i,U)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mor}_B(T,U)$$
is bijective. The colimit is a filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $B$ or $U$ is imposed.

proof.text: First suppose $g$ is locally of finite presentation. It is locally of finite type: on the affine neighbourhoods in the definition a finite polynomial presentation supplies finitely many algebra generators, giving the affine cover required for local finite type. No finiteness of an affine cover of $U$ or $B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, forward implication; the finite polynomial presentations of Tag 01TP imply local finite type.

proof.text: Fix an affine test system. Each $T_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the affine-scheme lemma. Write $T_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. By the spectrum correspondence these identifications carry every transition to a spectrum map; the spectrum-colimit lemma says these maps are affine. Thus the map-limit-factorization lemma applies to the given limit over $B$: every $B$-map $a:T\to U$ has the form $a_i\circ p_i$ for a $B$-map $a_i:T_i\to U$. This is the required existence of stage representatives.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, (1) implies (3), existence part (b), specialized to affine stages.

proof.text: Any two choices $a_i:T_i\to U$ and $b_j:T_j\to U$ for the same limit map have a common stage $k\ge i,j$. Their restrictions there are $B$-maps with equal pullbacks to $T$. The locally-finite-type equality lemma gives a further stage where they are equal (Step 1 supplies its local finite type hypothesis). Their coprojections to the set colimit are therefore equal. For each $a:T\to U$, choose the colimit class of any representative provided by Step 2. What we just proved makes this independent of the representative. It is inverse to the canonical map: its composite toward $\operatorname{Mor}_B(T,U)$ is $a$ by the factorization equation, and on every stage coprojection the other composite is the identity by independence. By the colimit universal property these equations prove bijectivity.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, (1) implies (3), uniqueness part (a), and assembly of the Hom-set colimit.

proof.text: Conversely assume the affine test map is bijective. Fix affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq U$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$ with $g(W)\subseteq V$. Given a directed system of $R$-algebras $A_i$ with colimit $A$ and a map $h:C\to A$, the spectrum correspondence gives a $V$-map $a:T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$. The spectrum-colimit lemma identifies $T$ with the limit of the affine $B$-schemes $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Apply the assumed surjectivity to $T\to W\to U$: it is $a_i\circ p_i$ for some $B$-map $a_i:T_i\to U$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proof of (2) implies (1), affine chart and directed algebra system.

proof.text: The open $a_i^{-1}(W)\subseteq T_i$ pulls back to all of $T$. The eventual-open-containment lemma applies because the stages are affine, hence quasi-compact, and their transitions are affine. It gives $j\ge i$ for which $a_i\circ(T_j\to T_i)$ has image in $W$. Restrict its continuous map and structure-sheaf map to the open subscheme $W$; this gives a unique map $a_j:T_j\to W$. Its composite to $B$ equals the given structure map. Both maps $T_j\to V$ obtained from this equality are equal because $V\hookrightarrow B$ is an inclusion of an open subscheme (restriction of the same space and sheaf map). Thus $a_j$ is a $V$-map, and its pullback to $T$ is $a$ since $W\hookrightarrow U$ is likewise an inclusion. The spectrum correspondence now gives an $R$-algebra map $h_j:C\to A_j$ with composite $h$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proof of (2) implies (1), eventual image containment in the affine open; Tag 01Z3 is replaced by its existing eventual-open-containment consequence.

proof.text: The construction in Steps 4 and 5 works for every directed $R$-algebra system and every map $C\to\varinjlim A_i$. The algebra directed-Hom criterion therefore makes $C$ finitely presented over $R$. Given any $u\in U$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $g(u)$ and an affine neighbourhood $W$ of $u$ inside $g^{-1}(V)$. The chart just proved finitely presented witnesses finite presentation at $u$ in the definition. Since $u$ was arbitrary, $g$ is locally of finite presentation, completing the converse without quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $U$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proof of (2) implies (1), application of Algebra Tag 00QO and the affine-local definition.
